approaches.sequence: Coming down the track from the Border road, the Hist crown shows first over the trees, then the lodge roof and the smoke from the common.
approaches.wayfinding: The track ends at the top of the village; the way runs down past the tree-minder's house to the common.

approaches.sequence: Walking up the footpath from the south-west, the spring house and the jars at its lip show first, then the Hist above it and the canoes on the bank beyond.
approaches.wayfinding: The footpath passes the spring house; the way up to the common leaves it just past the spring.

causalModel.founding: Founded at the Panther fork on springs that can be drunk unboiled.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The tribe is the interior's last friendly stop. Water is free; beds and rope are sold at high prices.
causalModel.pressures: The Hist is sick and the village blames salt from upstream. Traffic on the Helstrom track brings cult couriers and factors whom the tribe distrusts.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: Firm ground where clean water rises at a stone lip, at the last dry footing before the Helstrom approach.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: If the spring soured, the village would move within a season.

combatSpaces.why: The open common between the huts, where any fight in the village takes place.

districts.notes: One common with the Hist, the spring and the landing.

why.microGeography: A slope falling west to the channel; the huts sit on mud pads and the Hist on a mound.
why.playerPurpose: Beds and rope, free water, a trader and the shrine; the quests of the spring and the sick root start here.
why.what: A Hist village of seven buildings round an open common, with the spring house and the landing on the bank.
why.whyHere: Clean water rises here at the last dry ground before Helstrom.
why.whyNeighbours: It is the last friendly stop on the track to Helstrom; the refuge footpath runs along its bank.

landmarks.notes: The village's tribal Hist, ailing (MR01); hist-placement R2 tribal, R3 state sick.

why.microGeography: A raised mound of mud round its roots, on the slope above the channel.
why.playerPurpose: The landmark seen from the track; its sick root is the subject of MR01.
why.what: The village's Hist, a broad old tree whose roots are sickening.
why.whyHere: Most Argonian tribes build round their Hist; this village was founded at the spring and its tree.
why.whyNeighbours: The shrine is at its foot and the tree-minder's house beside it.
why.whySpot: On the mound above the common, where the slope levels before it falls to the water.

The footpath from the refuge comes up the channel bank and enters at the spring house.

approaches.sequence: Coming from the north-west, the hut domes and the landing lanterns show first; the road passes between the huts to the ford. The well roof shows across the water.
approaches.wayfinding: Follow the road through the landing to the ford; the poler's hut stands on the bank above it.

approaches.sequence: Coming down the road from the south-east, the station house roof and its smoke show first, then the well at the junction and the lean-to by the fire; the ford and the huts beyond open up at the junction.
approaches.wayfinding: The road runs past the yard wall to the well junction; the station house path leaves the street there.

causalModel.founding: A mixed village at the road's water point: an Imperial well on the south bench, an Argonian landing on the north bank across the ford. The landing is older than the station.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: Two communities share it because neither can hold the other's half.
causalModel.pressures: The well is Imperial-built and failing. The landing will not help to repair it in stone.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: A perennial spring beside a boat channel, where the road fords the water.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: Would become one community or two villages within a generation.

combatSpaces.why: The street between the well and the ford, where a road fight at the station happens.

districts.notes: The Argonian half on the north strip; no Hist (see siting).

why.whyNeighbours: It faces the well-station across the ford. It keeps no Hist: its people's tree stands at Fenmarch Village (place.imperial-fringe.fenmarch-village, 1.7 km). They go home for the hatching.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: type recipe road-station-village (a keeper and travellers); record occupants D1 family (few), D2 travellers (few); roster npcs.json well-keeper and poler
scaleGrounding.why: Two named keepers and one landing family live here; travellers come and go. Six buildings stand, three in the well-station and three in the landing; the dry ground holds no seventh. Beside them stand the well, the lean-to, the ferry raft and the dry-stone walls that hold the two station pads.
